thread:
Kevin: quick q — we have an internal feature that writes short-lived debug caches to redis with keys like user:<uid>:sess:<session_id>. The cache TTL is 10m. Do we need to scrub uid from the key or is TTL + redis eviction enough? Curious about logs/traces too — i think we log the error with the key in some places.
Maria: @Kevin we should assume any identifier in a log or key is PII unless proved otherwise. TTL helps but not sufficient for retention policy. Which logs contain the key?
Kevin: the app logs in the worker: 
```
logger.error("cache miss for key=%s", cache_key)
```
and the worker traces include cache keys in the span attributes.
Joni: short answer: redact at source. Replace uid with a hash or redact token before logging. For traces, prefer boolean flags or hashed ids (non-reversible) and document the transform so audits can verify.
Evan: adding infra flavour — if you keep keys in redis, we can't redact past writes. For cache keys, do either: 1) stop writing uid into the key, or 2) rotate/flush cluster on a retention event. But rotate is heavy. Hashing at write time is simplest.
Kevin: ok — for immediate fix i can change logger to not include raw key, and update spans. For redis keys, hashing sounds good. Any objection from privacy/legal? @Joni
Joni: no objection. Also add a migration note: any existing keys with raw uids need to be TTL-expired; maybe run a background job to sweep older keys older than X. Do we have metrics on how many keys exist?
Maria: we do, use redis-cli scan + count pattern user:* and filter by ttl. But beware prod cluster impact; do this on a replica or offline window.
AuditBot: NOTICE: request recorded — data handling change affecting PII in logs. Please file a confluence note and ping compliance for a short review.
Kevin: filing the note now. For sweep, thinking of a one-off job: iterate keys matching user:* and delete if ttl < 0 or created_at < 30d. Is deleting keys enough for compliance or do we need an audit trail?
Joni: deletion is okay for operational cleanup, but log entries and traces are separate. We need to issue a logs purge request if there are identified PII instances in centralized logging (sumologic/elk). Please open a ticket to seclogs with examples.
Evan: quick infra concern — the tracing system keeps indices for 90d. If we want to purge specific spans, we'll need to call the tracing retention API or ask the vendor. That can take time.
Kevin: thanks. Plan: 1) remove raw key from logs immediately (PR incoming), 2) switch key format to hashed uid (rollout plan), 3) open tickets for log + trace purge + confluence note. Will also schedule sweep on replica.
Maria: sounds good. Ping me when the PR is ready and include a migration checklist. :thumbsup:
Joni: also add unit tests to ensure log formatting doesn't accidentally include the uid.
Kevin: yup will add. ETA for PR later today.
Evan: LMK if you want a reserved window to run the sweep (avoid scan storms).
Kevin: will do, thanks all :pray:
